column1: ## Round 4 through `template.py learn` (the real API, claude-opus-5-5, effort medium, two attempts): every input
## through `provost --sync --llm` with a key and NO stored template (llm_round.sh --round4 --learn), 2026-10-27. Rated once,
## blind (raters saw only the input and the output), on CRITERIA.md. default = round 4's engine rating; helpers = the
## iterated helper-written templates (ratings-llm-templates-f2.tsv). The templates are in llm-templates-learn/.

column9: note

All 4 listed packages (with their section), the upgraded/installed/removed/not-upgraded summary and all 6 Inst/Conf actions with version, archives and arch land in correct columns; only the content-free 'Reading package lists...' progress lines are dropped.

Summary line (7 shift/reduce, -Wconflicts-sr), all 7 conflicts with token and example, and all 28 shift/reduce derivation steps with conflict, level, rule and production are kept in stable columns; only alignment whitespace is collapsed (which symbol a level-1 step expands is recoverable from the example).

Every section survives as its own dataset with correct counts: 4 state conflicts, 14 grammar rules, 13 terminals, 5 nonterminals with on-left/on-right rules, 8 state items with lookaheads and 16 state actions; the only omission is the redundant '(lhs)' after 'reduce using rule N', which the grammar dataset already gives.

Lossless but unstructured: text-lines files every line as a single column, so each of the 2 failures (test name, Expected/Received, location, duration) is split over about 12 rows of code context, and the pass/skip/todo/fail/expect counts are not parsed into fields.

Text-lines dump: every line is kept but as one column, so keys and values (Bundler 4.0.9, Ruby 3.3.6p108, Git SHA ...) are not separated, and the stripped indentation loses which sub-keys (Platforms, Full Path, Gem Home, Git, RVM ...) belong to which parent.
All 59 AST nodes are one row each, with the filtered function, correct depth, parent address, node kind, address, source range, location and details; the tree shape is fully recoverable.

All 106 timer rows across the 7 report sections are kept with section and name, and User/System/User+System/Wall times and percentages are mapped correctly even in the 4-column sections; all 6 'Total Execution Time' lines are in a separate dataset.

All record layout fields, sizes, record and field decls, LLVM types and both bitfield infos are correct, but each bitfield's ConstantExpr/IntegerLiteral subtree (6 node lines, with addresses and source ranges) is reduced to a BitWidth value and the RecordDecl 'definition' token is dropped.
All 36 trace lines are split into file, line, command and args (the help text glued onto line 1 is kept in a trailing column), and all 10 '--' status messages are in their own dataset.
The version and release time, all 11 options (short/long/description) and all 34 commands with aliases split out are correct, but the 'Usage: command [options] [arguments]' synopsis line is dropped.
All 3 legend lines land in a color/meaning table and all 106 warning flags in one row each with correct depth and parent derived from the indentation tree; nothing lost.

All 26 TERM/COLORTERM filters, 18 file-type entries and 5 extensions land with keyword, color and comment in the right columns, but the LINK entry's continuation comment line (' # numerical value, the color is as for the file pointed to.)') is dropped, leaving its comment cut off mid-sentence (the commented-out #NORMAL/#FILE/#.cmd entries and prose comments are also not kept).
All 8 summary key-values land in one wide row under their own names and all 5 histogram rows keep range start/end, free extents, free blocks and percent under the input's headers; nothing lost.

All 43 pattern elements land under their own names in one row and all 50 charset pages split cleanly into page + 8 words, but the summary line 'Pattern has 43 elts (size 48)' is dropped and every value's type/binding suffix ((s) strong vs (w) weak, (i)/(f)) is stripped, losing the weak/strong binding information.

Source header, all 3 function summaries (called/returned/blocks), all 26 annotated source lines (count, line number, source text with indentation) and all 11 branch records (tied to their function and line, taken count, fallthrough/never-executed note) are kept in four well-named tables; nothing lost.

All 5 function and 2 file records land one per row with lines/branches/taken/calls percent and totals plus the .gcov output name, and the overall 73.33% of 30 total is kept, but util.c's 'No calls' line is not recorded (its calls columns are just blank, indistinguishable from the functions where calls were never reported, rather than 0).
All 8 top-level fields (display/edit name, type, size, uri, local path, unix mount) land in one named row and all 48 attributes split cleanly into namespace, attribute and value; nothing lost.

WORK, the modinfo blob, 11 executed commands (env/command/args/# internal note) and all 62 packagefile lines are kept cleanly, but the two heredoc commands writing $WORK/b001/importcfg and importcfg.link are dropped and the packagefile rows carry no column saying which config they belong to, so the 5 compile imports and 57 link imports are merged into one list with fmt/os/sort/strings/runtime duplicated unexplained.

Package/import/synopsis and the 9 declarations' kind, receiver, name, signature and first doc paragraph are right, but Ring's struct body lines and Link's 2nd and 3rd doc paragraphs were turned into spurious columns (_Value, _//, }, If, If_2) whose values are copied onto every declaration, so New/Do/Len/Move/etc. all falsely carry Link's paragraphs and Ring's fields while Link's own doc is cut to its first paragraph.

Read as YAML into one 110-column row: each linter's description survives under its name, but the 'Enabled by your configuration' and 'Disabled by your configuration' section headers are dropped so the 5 enabled linters are indistinguishable from the 105 disabled ones, each linter is a column rather than a row with name/description/tags, and the 'wsl [deprecated]' entry is lost entirely.

Every line's text survives in order, but it was filed as raw text-lines in a single column, so each of the 9 diagnostics is split over 3 rows (message, source line, caret with its indentation stripped) and file/line/col/message/linter are never parsed into columns, and the 9-issues per-linter summary is left as unparsed text rows.

The flat profile (4 rows) and the 5 primary call-graph entries are correct, but the 8 caller/callee lines are filed in a separate table with no link to the entry they belong to or whether they are caller or callee (so who-calls-whom is lost and values like scan 0.71 read as scan's own time), main's <spontaneous> caller is dropped, the function index is filed as 2 rows with empty index and name (its 4 entries are lost), and the 'Each sample counts as 0.01 seconds' and granularity lines with numbers are dropped.

The entry (vt220, alias vt200, description DEC VT220) and all 107 capabilities land one per row with terminal/capability/type/value, booleans, numerics and string escapes kept exactly; only the infocmp '# Reconstructed via infocmp from file' comment line is dropped.

All 90 log lines are accounted for: 16 gc,init settings as one named row, 5 pauses with heap before/after/capacity/duration, 25 phase timings, 20 region transitions (empty target where the input has none), 5 cpu rows and 19 other events with uptime/level/tags/GC id, all under correct columns; only the per-line uptime and tag of the init settings are not kept.

The class header, all 8 members with descriptors, all 71 bytecode instructions (member/offset/opcode/operands/comment), the 2-row exception table and all 13 LineNumberTable entries are filed with correct columns and each row tied to its member.

All nine sections survive with correctly named columns: total usage, the 3 per-type usage rows with every value and percentage, virtual space, 45 chunk-freelist rows ((none) as count 0) plus 3 totals, the 5 waste rows, the header pool, 13 internal statistics and the 10 settings; only the leading '20907:' pid header and the waste note's 'total committed size 4.06 MB' (repeated in virtual_space) are not kept.

All 13 events are filed: 6 GCHeapMemoryPoolUsage and 7 ThreadStart rows with every field (thread names and javaThreadIds split out, N/A parent kept), plus 6 stack frames tied to their event id with method and line; only the '...' truncation marker on the first stack trace is not kept.
The recording header (Version 2.1, Chunks 1, Start, Duration 20 s) is one row and all 52 event types land with Event_Type/Count/Size_(bytes) under the input's own header names.

The pid, JVM version, GC type and thread count, all 12 heap-configuration settings and the 4 heap-usage spaces (regions/capacity/used/free/used_%) are filed correctly, but the 'Server compiler detected.' and 'using thread-local object allocation.' lines are dropped, as is the 'G1 Young Generation' grouping that puts Eden and Survivor under it.

All 21 plugins land one per row with Option/Argument/Description and multi-line descriptions joined intact, but the trailing section explaining the <pattern-list> forms (<glob-pattern>, glob:, regex:, @<filename>) is dropped entirely.

All 26 threads (17 Java + 9 VM, including the nameless truncated one) carry correct named fields, all 68 stack/lock/info lines sit under the right thread with kinds, and the timestamp/JVM and JNI refs counts are kept, but the 'Threads class SMR info' section is dropped (_java_thread_list=0x00007f3394001d80, length=17; its element addresses survive only as the threads' tids).

Both sections survive as named tables, all 19 CPUs and all 52 features each one row with name and description in stable columns; only the generic two-line usage footer ('Use +feature to enable...') is dropped, which is boilerplate help text rather than target data.

Executable, breakpoint (module/where/file/line/column/address), process launch/stop/exit events, frames, frame variables, image list and source listing are all kept with correct fields, but the struct_members table merges the two printed structs into 8 rows with no column saying which expression/type each member belongs to (p *it as 'const item' vs p *it->next as 'item' is lost), and the source lines lose their code indentation.

File/format, the compile-unit header (all 8 fields), all 31 DIEs with offset/depth/tag and all 124 attributes keyed by die_offset/tag/attribute/value are present and correctly placed; only the six NULL child-terminator entries are dropped, whose nesting information is carried by the depth column.

Summary (9 metrics), both legends, the 5-instruction info table (with the MayStore '*' correctly under MayStore for vmovss), per-iteration pressure and by-instruction pressure all survive with real resource names (JALU0..JVIMUL) applied as columns and every value in its correct position.

File info, the full ElfHeader (Ident fields flattened into one row, all 21 fields correct) and all 7 sections present in the (truncated) input are one row each with every field under its name; per-flag hex values (SHF_ALLOC (0x2)) are reduced to names but remain derivable from the kept Flags total.

The 4 build steps (step/total/description), all 7 metrics rows with their real header names and the hash-load summary (0.61, 156 entries, 257 buckets) are correctly structured, but the 'ninja: Entering directory `build'' line is dropped, losing the build directory.

All 15 GC trace events are one row each with pid, isolate, time, type, before/after heap and committed sizes, pooled, pause/external ms, mu values and reason correctly split, but the interleaved program output line 'kept 2667' (a line carrying a number) is dropped.

All 47 ops are one row each with seq, class, op, flags and next correctly split, but the optree's nesting (encoded only by indentation) is discarded with no depth/parent column so the tree cannot be reconstructed, and the 'tally.pl syntax OK' status line is dropped.

Filed as text-lines: every input line is one row in a single positional column, so the benchmark tables are not extracted at all (method, ops/sec and usecs/op are fused in one string, the five section headings and their parenthetical notes sit interleaved as data rows with two notes split across rows, and no row carries its section), leaving the output no more structured than the raw input.

All 15 histogram buckets (bound, percent, count) and the per-loop-time summary are filed correctly, but the preamble 'Testing timing overhead for 2 seconds' (the test duration, a number-carrying line) is dropped and the '< us' header loses its '<' upper-bound sense.

Class header, all five section counts, all seven methods (section, origin, modifiers, return type and kind) and all five parameters (method, position, required, type, name) are filed with real names and nothing lost.
All five errors land one per row with severity, message, line and file in stable columns, and the 'Tally.pod has 5 pod syntax errors' summary is kept as its own row.

All 80 headerless tab-separated rows are filed byte-identical with sensible pg_settings-style column names (name, context, category, vartype, boot_val, min_val, max_val, short_desc, extra_desc), empty fields preserved.
The single process record is filed as one row with all 32 fields (IDs, page faults, CPU times, memory, pointers, scheduling) under names qualified by their section, every value correct.

Module name, summary, reference URL, file, the six functions and the __all__ data entry are correct, but the sections dataset shreds the MODULE REFERENCE and DESCRIPTION prose: first words of lines become column names (source, are, rgb_to_abc(r, ...) and are lost from the text, and each section's row carries the other section's lines, so the description is misattributed.

All 18 formatters land one per row with names, full description and filename patterns split out correctly, but the 'Pygments version 2.21.0, (c) 2006-present ...' banner line carrying the version is dropped.

Session info, progress line, all 7 short-summary entries and the 1 failed/4 passed/1 skipped/1 xfailed/0.03s totals are correct, but the reports dataset uses junk column names (+, +_2, +_3, an empty name, >) for test_rounding's assertion explanation and source lines and copies those values into the test_germany and test_france pass rows, attributing the failure detail to tests that passed.
All 84 lines of the AST dump become one row each with depth, ancestor path, field name, node type and literal value, every node and leaf (constants, names, empty lists) preserved in order.

All five frames (file, line, function, code, traceback number) and all three exceptions with message and the chain sentence linking each to the previous are filed; only the caret marker lines, which are decoration, are dropped.

All 55 opcodes land one per row with offset, code, opcode and argument in stable columns (non-ASCII string intact) and the 'highest protocol' summary line is kept as a field/value row; only the nesting indentation is dropped, which is fully implied by the MARK opcodes and their '(MARK at N)' arguments.
All 14 classes (name, bases, line) and all 69 methods (owning class, name, line) are filed in two well-named tables with every value under the right column and nothing dropped.

All five warnings land one per row with file, line, category, message and the source line kept together in named columns, and the ResourceWarning tracemalloc hint is kept intact (category + message) in a separate notes dataset; nothing is lost.
All 6 entries are filed under the real File_Name/Modified/Size headers with the date-time kept whole and the space-containing and non-ASCII filenames intact.

Every section survives in properly named tables: 13 progress lines (percent, type, key, size, unit), the 6 biggest-key lines, sampled-keys count, total/avg key length and the 6 per-type totals with count, size, unit, percent and avg; only the instructional comment banner is dropped.

All 7 samples are filed under the real column names (keys, mem, clients, blocked, requests, connections, child) with values correctly aligned and the empty child column kept; only the data/load/child group banner is dropped, and the request delta stays with its total as printed.

All 35 instructions (pos, insn, operands, line, events), both local-table headers and all 5 locals are filed in correct columns, but the six '== disasm: #<ISeq:...>' section headers are dropped and the iseq column is empty in every row, so no instruction or local can be attributed to its method (<main>, <class:Cart>, initialize, add, count, block in count) or source range.

Every section is kept: speed/rows/columns/line as a named settings row, all 17 control characters as named columns, and all 53 flags one per row with the leading '-' correctly turned into enabled yes/no.
All 45 syscalls across the 8 groups land one per row with their @group and the group's description comment attached in stable named columns; nothing is lost.
All 6 [EXTENDED] entries are filed with type, overridden path and drop-in target in named columns, and the '6 overridden configuration files found' summary is kept as a numeric field/value row.

All 56 option lines land as one row each with option and value columns, quoted values (including the long status-format strings and escaped quotes) kept verbatim, and option+value reproduces the input exactly.

Summary (pid, version, command, 2 errors/2 contexts, 1/1 suppressed), both thread announcements, both races (access, size, address, thread, locks held, conflicting access, address description) and all 30 stack frames keyed to their thread/race context are correctly structured, but the guest program's own output line '2000' (the final counter value) is dropped, along with the two advisory hint lines.

All 24 timing lines are one row each with clock, self+sourced (blank where absent) and the event/script text, but the input's two-layout header is only half applied: the 15 non-sourcing lines' 'elapsed' times are filed under the sourcing layout's 'self' column with no elapsed column, the script column keeps the 'sourcing ' prefix, and the 'times in msec' unit line is dropped.

Document properties (version, encoding, URL, standalone), all 31 tree nodes (one row each with type, name, compact flag, depth, an XPath-style path and the exact content including whitespace-only text, the escaped UTF-8 name and the CDATA) and the x namespace declaration on /order are all kept in three well-named datasets.

All 105 field lines are kept in order with correct offset, field name, hex value and decoded text (including the [Bits 1-2] sub-flag, payload previews and the UTF-8 filename), but the added Record/Parent grouping is broken: after each LOCAL HEADER's first six fields the Record key switches to 'CRC', then 'UID', then 'GID' (74 of 105 rows, including every Filename), and UID/GID lose their Extra ID #0002 parent while GID Size is parented to 'UID', so each local header is split into four mislabelled pseudo-records.

All 11 error-log entries land one per row under the input's own headers (IDENTIFIER, TIMESTAMP, T, C, RESOURCE_NAME, DESCRIPTION) with multi-word descriptions kept whole and every value matching the input.

All 28 headerless attribute lines land one per row under apt names (attribute, value, description, user_settable) matching lsattr's own -H header, with the empty location value correctly left blank, multi-word descriptions kept whole and True/True+/False flags intact.

All 38 key/value status lines become one wide record with each key as a column (END APC as END_APC) and every value intact including units, timestamps with offsets, multi-word strings and the 'FW:T2' colon inside FIRMWARE; only trailing padding is trimmed.

All 12 MAC entries land one per row under the input's headers (Vlan, Mac Address, Type, Ports) with values in the right columns, and the 'Total Mac Addresses for this criterion: 12' summary is kept as its own dataset; only the prompt echo, title and rule lines are dropped.

Both sections survive: the CPU utilization line is one record with five-second total and interrupt (23%/7%), one-minute and five-minute values under clear names, and all 14 processes land one per row under the input's headers with multi-word process names kept whole; only the prompt echo is dropped.

Pool status kv (all 9 fields), pool ServerSide traffic (7 stats), per-member status (3 members x 5 fields) and per-member ServerSide/General traffic (18 rows) are all present under the input's own labels with pool/member keys; only the prompt echo and rule lines are dropped.

All 10 fields land one per row with domain, type, charset, nullability, default, collation and check (the wrapped COLLATE and CHECK continuation lines are folded into their field), plus all 4 constraints with type/columns/definition and both triggers with sequence/type/status; only the SQL> prompts are dropped.

Runner version/revision/host/token/system ID, all 5 sections with start/end timestamps, duration and title, all 21 output/command lines tagged by section with line numbers (pytest failure and its 1 failed/15 passed/1 skipped summary kept verbatim), and the final ERROR exit code 1 are all present; ANSI/section markers are decoration.

Controller (model, slot, Embedded, serial), 2 drive cages, 2 ports, 2 arrays with type and unused space, 3 logical drives with size/RAID/status, all 8 physical drives with array (incl. Unassigned), port/box/bay, type, size, status and the spare flag, and the SEP enclosure's vendor/model/380/WWID are all present in correctly named columns.

All 6 disks land one per row under the real header names with each device's continuation line folded in as Block_Device and Raw_Device columns, so the two-line records stay together and nothing is lost.

Schedd name/address/timestamp, all 5 batches under the real OWNER..JOB_IDS header (ID:/DAG: batch names and _ placeholders intact), and both Total lines decomposed into jobs/completed/removed/idle/running/held/suspended are all present.

Filed as text-lines into a single column A, so the 13-row interface table is never parsed: its header (Interface/PHY/Protocol/InUti/OutUti/inErrors/outErrors) is not applied, every row is one unsplit raw string, and the leading indentation marking GE0/0/1 and GE0/0/2 as Eth-Trunk1 members is trimmed away; the legend lines are likewise unstructured.

System name, date/time and all 14 status/auxiliary-storage values land in one kv row under their labels, and the 4 pool rows sit under correctly merged two-line headers (Pool_Size_(M), DB_Fault, Non-DB_Pages, Act-Wait...) including the +++++ overflow value; only the function-key/command screen chrome is dropped.

Dbspaces (5 rows) and Chunks (6 rows) are correctly columned and the capacity-mode setting is kept, but the banner line (Version 14.10.FC10, On-Line, Up 12 days 04:21:07, 2124368 Kbytes) is dropped entirely, the two 'N active, M maximum' rows in counts carry no indication of which section (dbspaces vs chunks) they belong to, and the Metadata row is not tied to its chunk 5.

All five sections survive with their real headers: model (1 row), apps (4, telegraf's empty Version kept blank), units (4, leader asterisks kept), machines (4) and offer (1), every value under the right column and blank Message cells preserved.

All 29 interface/address lines land as rows under the real header columns, with continuation lines (extra inet6 addresses, multiservice, the four sp-0/0/0.16383 local/remote pairs) correctly filled down with their interface, admin, link and proto; only the CLI prompt, {master:0} and the --> arrows (decoration) are dropped.

The 14 klog events each land as one row with severity/date/time/pid/file/line/message/attributes correct, but the fatal event's multi-line err=< ... > body was turned into two bogus columns named 'failed' and '>' (eating the word 'failed') and that error text is stamped onto all 14 rows, so 13 unrelated events falsely carry the Kubelet fatal error while row 14's own attributes hold only 'err=<'.

All three tables (5 instance groups, 6 node statuses, 3 validation errors) are filed as separate datasets with their real headers and correct values, and the cluster name and final 'Error: validation failed: cluster not yet healthy' are kept as kv; only section titles, blank lines and the 'Validation Failed' verdict (restated by the Error line) are dropped.

All 18 taxa land as rows with percent, clade reads, taxon reads, rank code, taxid and name under correct kraken2 column names; the name indentation is stripped but the rank codes keep the hierarchy recoverable, and the two extra Minimizers columns are merely empty.

All 41 key/value pairs are filed as one record with the real key names as columns and values intact (including the full byte/512-unit size strings); only the 'This disk is an APFS Volume. APFS Information:' section intro is dropped, whose content is restated by the APFS fields.

All 18 registry nodes land as rows with name, @location, class, id, state flags, busy count/time and retain split cleanly (including the !registered node and the non-ASCII name), but the tree depth/parent relationships drawn by the +-o/| indentation are lost, so you can no longer tell which interface or device hangs off which hub or controller.

All 36 scalar attributes are filed as one record keyed by attribute name and all 12 items of the 5 list-valued attributes (Authors, ContentTypeTree, EncodingApplications, UsedDates, WhereFroms) as attribute/value rows, with UTF-8 values and (null) preserved; the only nit is that _kMDItemDisplayNameWithExtensions lost its leading underscore in the column name.

The template was declined and the text-lines fallback files every line as one undifferentiated column: the four '== Device Types/Runtimes/Devices/Device Pairs ==' section headers are dropped so device types, runtimes, devices and pairs are indistinguishable, devices are not tied to their '-- runtime --' group, nothing (name, UDID, state, availability) is split into fields, and the device-pair record is split across three rows.

All 7 interfaces are filed as one row each with their wrapped continuation lines merged, the item number, flags and ;;; comments in their own columns and every key=value under its real key name; only the CLI prompt and the flag-legend line are dropped.

All 8 sessions land as rows under the real sp_who2 headers with values correctly aligned (HostName/BlkBy '.', BlkBy 54 on SPID 57, multi-word Command and ProgramName kept whole, empty ProgramName for system SPIDs); only the dash rule and the redundant duplicate SPID column (identical values) are dropped.

All 7 two-line sessions are kept together as one row each, with the stacked header split into named columns (ID, Application, State, Type, Flag, Src/Sport/Zone/Proto, translated IP/port, Vsys, Dst/Dport/Zone, translated IP/port) and every value under the right name, including the blank Flag cells.

The metrics table is reproduced exactly (3 rows, all 35 named columns, including the empty SAMPLE/LIBRARY/READ_GROUP cells), but the header section is dropped: the CollectAlignmentSummaryMetrics command line (input BAM, output, GRCh38 reference, options), the 'Started on' timestamp and the METRICS CLASS name are not filed anywhere.

All 21 lines are kept with correct fields (started/processing/completed requests parsed into method, path, IP, controller, action, status, timings; other lines with severity, timestamp, PID, request ID), but the FATAL event is split: its row in log_entries has an empty Message while the NoMethodError text and its two backtrace frames sit as four separate rows in a separate continuation_lines dataset, linked only by request ID.
All 6 hosts (global plus five nodes) are filed under the input's own 11 column names with every value in place, including the '-' placeholders for global and node04; only the rule line is dropped.

Nothing is structured: all three tables (database row, device_fragments, device/segment) and the 'log only free kbytes = 0' pair are filed as 19 raw lines in a single column A, with header and rule lines stored as data rows and no value placed under any column name.

All 29 log lines are kept as one row each across four consistent datasets (build-level lines, 3 step headers with step number, total, name and the 1s duration, 15 block lines with time, W/E status, block and message, and 8 ##teamcity service messages split into type, name, duration, message, details and flowId), with every value under the right column.

Held in 'unsorted' with no dataset filed, so none of the six pipe-separated client records (clid, cid, client_database_id, client_nickname, client_type) nor the 'error id=0 msg=ok' status line was extracted.

The 6-row result keeps its 4 named columns with correct values (including the '?' null and '.00'), and the session (BTEQ version, start time, PID, release/version, BTET, UTF8, RC 0) and query (SQL, 6 rows, 4 columns, 2 seconds) are filed, but the .LOGON target 'tdprod/etl_reader', the logon's 'Total elapsed time was 1 second' line, and the logon-success / logoff / exit status lines are dropped.

All three entries are filed one row each with the input's own keys as columns (Boot Manager in one dataset, both Boot Loaders together in another), every value under the right key, and the two-line displayorder kept together as one value.

Every section is kept with Computer/User scope: the RSOP summary (created-on, user, computer, mode, OS and profile fields), both settings blocks (DN, last applied, DC, threshold, domain), all 6 applied GPOs, all 3 filtered GPOs with their filtering reason and WMI filter, and all 22 security groups; only the tool banner and copyright line are dropped.

All 5 sessions land as one row each under the real header names, with blank SESSIONNAME kept as empty cells, the '>' current-session marker split into its own column, and the multi-word IDLE TIME and LOGON TIME values intact.

Every section is kept across six datasets: the job header key-values, all 4 directories, all 8 file lines with their parent directory carried down, the multi-line ERROR 32 event as one row (time, code, path, message, retry), the Dirs/Files/Bytes/Times summary with the sparse Times values under the right columns (FAILED, Extras), and the Speed/Ended totals.

All 3 task records come out as one row each with all 29 keys as named columns plus the Folder context, and every value, including the quoted Task To Run command and the comma-bearing Power Management and Idle Time values, sits under its own key.

All 18 processes land with the 10 real header names, and every multi-word value (Image Name 'System Idle Process', User Name, Status 'Not Responding', the window titles with spaces, pipes and Unicode) sits whole under the right column.

23 privileges are parsed correctly under Privilege_Name/Description/State, but the 24th and last row (SeDelegateSessionUserImpersonatePrivilege, 'Obtain an impersonation token for another user in the same session', Disabled) is dropped, probably because its name fills the column to the full width with no gap.

All 7 connections land under the #fields names with every value in place, and the separator/path/open/close header lines are kept as a metadata dataset, but the #types line (time, string, addr, port, ... set[string]), which gives each column's type, is dropped.

The 3 catalog entries are tidied well as entry/section/key/value (including the flag list and the SYSTEM-TIMESTAMP split over two lines), and the 14 entry counts and 2 IDC messages are kept, but the summary line 'THE NUMBER OF PROTECTED ENTRIES SUPPRESSED WAS 0' and the LISTCAT ENTRIES(...) ALL command echo are dropped, and the cluster's PROTECTION-PSWD/RACF are wrongly filed under the SMSDATA section.
